{
  "summary": "The nervous system functions by coordinating sensation, movement, and internal regulation via interacting cells and circuits, comprising the central nervous system (brain and spinal cord) and peripheral nervous system. Information flows through sensory pathways to the CNS and motor pathways to effectors, while neurons utilize dendrites, cell bodies, and axons for signal reception, processing, and transmission, respectively; however, a neuron's specific contribution is determined by its circuitry",
  "topics": [
    "Nervous system coordination of sensation, movement, and internal regulation",
    "Central nervous system composition (brain and spinal cord)",
    "Peripheral nervous system function connecting to the body",
    "Sensory pathways carrying information toward the CNS",
    "Motor pathways carrying commands to muscles or glands",
    "Neuron structure: dendrites receiving signals, cell body supporting activity, axon carrying signals",
    "Variation in neuron shape and connectivity",
    "Neuron contribution dependent on connections and circuit activity rather than shape alone"
  ]
}
